intro_sketch: Drawing has always been one of those fine arts that fascinates me and that I want to practise myself. It is not the final product that captures my attention, but the process of creating it: seeing the object of a drawing as a combination of form, shape, line and flow, light and shade. It is also the ability to simply sit down quietly and focus on the making and the practising. The eye-hand coordination is absorbing: you get lost in the drawing itself, so focused on getting it right that you never rush, get bored or get frustrated, because you enjoy the process of moving your hand, checking with your eye how it looks, and iterating until you like it.
intro_poetry: Poetry, to me, is the expression of one's experience and state of emotion in a structured way. Searching for the words to describe what I feel at that moment, then building the verse so that it rhymes in a poetic form of choice, is truly satisfying. It is like solving a puzzle. In fact, it is like engineering. Unfortunately, my poems are written in my language, Khmer, because it is the language that comes most naturally to me. In fact, it seems the language itself was made for poetry, only that nobody notices.
